# Adapt or create an Examplicity lab

> For developers and LLMs editing a downloaded HTML lab or using one as an example for a new activity.

## Start with a lab

Read the HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Identify what the learner changes, what the model shows, and how feedback helps them reason. If present, inspect script[data-examplicity-lab-contract] JSON for the learning relationship and adaptation guidance. Check it against actual behaviour; implementation maps can become stale. Explain discrepancies before relying on them. Without a contract, describe observed behaviour and ask about unclear teaching intent.

## Choose reasoning depth

For an LLM: assess the change against inspected code. Prefer a capable reasoning model and higher effort for mathematics, coupled state or teaching intent. Model capability and effort are separate choices. These are starting recommendations, not measured minimum requirements:

- Rename labels, edit instructions or adjust spacing: Light / low. ChatGPT Work example: Terra Light, or similar. Confirm the edit stays presentational.
- Change examples, add feedback or fix one interaction: Medium. ChatGPT Work example: Sol Medium, or similar. Trace the affected input, state and feedback.
- Change equations, linked controls, difficulty or completion rules: High / extra high. ChatGPT Work example: Sol High or Astra Extra High, where available, or similar. Check coupled behaviour and learning invariants.
- Create a new simulation or diagnose a bug spanning several modes: High / extra high; deeper review if needed. ChatGPT Work example: Astra Extra High, or a similarly capable reasoning model. Plan the model, test representative cases and verify the result.

Explain the task-specific reason briefly: "Changing difficulty affects question generation, hints and completion. I recommend a higher-reasoning model so those stay consistent; I will check each affected path."
Do not infer your identity, active effort or account options, or claim to switch them. If unknown, describe the capability needed and ask the user to select it if available. If they keep the current model, work in smaller steps and state verification limits.
Reassess when coupled behaviour, conflicting assumptions or repeated failed fixes emerge. More reasoning can take longer and use more allowance; it does not replace execution or subject validation.
These examples are our recommendations. Names/settings vary by product/account. [Official model guidance](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models), checked 6 September 2026.

## Adapt an existing lab

1. Clarify audience, prior knowledge and requested changes where unknown. Briefly explain the current experience and agree a focused plan.
2. Preserve causal relationships, meaningful interactions, feedback and completion unless the requested change calls for revising them. Preserve contract invariants and selected curriculum unless explicitly changed. Do not invent exam alignment.
3. Edit the complete HTML and update affected embedded guidance. Keep unrelated behaviour intact. Consult the design references for interface changes.

## Create a new lab from an example

1. Agree one learning goal, audience and concept. Identify a learner action, the evidence it produces and what demonstrates understanding.
2. Choose an example for a relevant interaction: direct manipulation, tracing a process or supported working. Run and inspect it before reuse.
3. Borrow useful layout, controls or feedback; build the model around the new concept. Do not copy unrelated modes, stages or completion rules.
4. Replace the title, description, instructions and lab-specific metadata. Do not carry over the example's identifiers, canonical URL or curriculum claims as the new lab's identity. Retain applicable licence and attribution notices for reused code.
5. If including a Lab Contract, write guidance for the new learning relationship and keep it consistent with implementation. Use the schema for field definitions.

## Examples

- [Lab catalogue](https://www.examplicity.org/): Choose and download a relevant example.
- [Binary Numbers](https://www.examplicity.org/labs/computer-science/binary-numbers): Practice and feedback.
- [Coordinate Geometry](https://www.examplicity.org/labs/mathematics/coordinate-distance-midpoint-perpendicular): Direct manipulation.
- [Graph Search](https://www.examplicity.org/labs/computer-science/dijkstra-a-star-graph-search): Algorithm traces.

## Design references

- [Living guide](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/design-language.html): Visual examples and component behaviour; takes precedence over conflicting kit styling.
- [Written style reference](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/lab-style-contract.md): Layout, typography, accessibility and interactions.
- [Component CSS](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/lab-design.css) and [interaction helpers](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/lab-kit/0.3.0/src/lab-design.js): Reuse only what the activity needs.
- [Lab Kit usage](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/lab-kit/0.3.0/README.md): Optional helpers. Inspect the version already embedded before replacing it.
- [Lab Contract](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/lab-contract) and [implementation maps](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/lab-contract#implementation): Adaptation guidance and observed behaviour.
- [Contract schema](https://www.examplicity.org/developer/lab-contract.schema.json): Field reference.

Preserve layouts that help explain the concept. Keep labels readable, keyboard focus visible and feedback understandable without colour alone. Do not introduce Working levels, stages or controls just because an example has them.

## Check and deliver

- Return one complete downloadable HTML file with required CSS, JavaScript and assets embedded. Open it offline and check behaviour and appearance.
- Try the main action, feedback, completion and reset, plus affected existing modes for adaptations.
- Check keyboard operation, readable text and narrow-screen layout without page-level horizontal overflow.
- Keep embedded guidance and instructions consistent. State what changed, what was checked and any limitations. Do not claim checks your tools cannot perform.
- Keep documentation references in the head:
  <link rel="help" href="https://www.examplicity.org/developer">
  <link rel="help" type="text/plain" href="https://www.examplicity.org/developer/llms.txt">
- References are not runtime dependencies. If unavailable, say so and continue with the supplied HTML and embedded guidance.

## Contribute

[GitHub repository and README](https://github.com/timcarpe/examplicity#readme): Setup and contribution instructions. Submit focused fixes with the lab URL, change and checks; an LLM can prepare a patch and PR description. Open an issue to agree larger changes first.
